title.narrative: Agricultural Value Chain Competitiveness and Safety

description.narrative: The project will strengthen value chains of competitive agricultural products (CAPs) cassava, mangoes, cashew nuts, vegetables, and native chicken in the provinces of Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Oddar Meanchey, Preah Vihear, Siem Reap, and Tboung Khmum. The project will (i) facilitate access to credit for agro-enterprises and agricultural cooperatives; (ii) promote viable market links among agro-enterprises and agricultural cooperatives, and enhance food safety and quality; and (iii) improve farm-to-market connectivity. The project will benefit 230 agricultural cooperatives (about 27,000 households) and about 50 agribusinesses in the project areas, and the number of beneficiaries will be expanded through intermediary financing.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Agricultural value chain connectivity enhanced Indicator: About 3,000 road safety training participants, of which at least 50% are female, reported increased knowledge on the subject (baseline: 0, 0%). Achievement: 4479 Progress/Status: Road safety training is completed in six target provinces, namely, Preah Vihear, Kampong Cham, Kampong Thom, Tboung Khmum, Siem Reap, and Oddar Meanchey with 4,479 participants, of which 2,276 are women (51%) reported increased knowledge after training from 56% at the pre-test to 88% at the post-test. Among them, it was reported that women increased knowledge after the training from 55% at the pre-test to 89% at the post-test. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain connectivity enhanced Indicator: At least 130 km of farm-to-market roads improved and climate-proofed to enhance connectivity between farms and markets (2020 baseline: 0 km). (RFI B) Achievement: 115.5 Progress/Status: The rehabilitation of 115.55 km of farm-to-market roads (FMRs) across the six target provinces has been completed, achieving 100% physical progress.
The Ministry of Rural Development (MRD) signed a contract with the selected contractor for additional FMRs totaling 25.24 km in January 2026 with the valued of $4,741,039.88. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least $40 million in AVC loans and equity capital loans provided to eligible borrowers, of which at least 25% ($10.0 million) is provided to women-owned PAEs and female borrowers (female farmers) (2020 baseline: $0, 0%) Achievement: 24139178 Progress/Status: Loans have been disbursed to 1,064 sub-borrowers, amounting to a total of $24.14 million, representing 60% of the total loan allocation of $40 million.
Of this amount, Sathapana Bank (SPNB) disbursed $15.05 million to 909 borrowers, while ARDB disbursed $9.085 million to 155 borrowers. Borrowers include producers of cassava (370), mango (46), cashew nut (475), vegetables (112), and native chickens (61). Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least 40% of AVC loan recipients are micro, small and medium-sized PAEs (2020 baseline: 0) (RFI A) Achievement: 99 Progress/Status: Of the 1.064 sub-loans disbursed, 191 were provided to participating agro-enterprises (PAEs). Of these, 189 sub-loans were extended to micro, small, and medium PAEs, representing 99% of loans to all PAE sub-borrowers. The remaining 684 loans were disbursed to individual farmers. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain financing enhanced Indicator: At least 50 government and PFI staff, of which at least 25% are female, report increased knowledge on AVC financing and credit guarantee and green financing (2020 baseline: 0, 0%) Achievement: 514 Progress/Status: A total of 514 participants from government agencies and participating financial institutions (PFIs) have enhanced their knowledge of agricultural value chain (AVC) financing and credit guarantee mechanisms. Among them, 93 participants (18.1%) are women. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: About 230 PACs established IBPs with PAEs, of which at least 20% of PACs established contract farming arrangements or other alternative arrangements such as seasonal sales agreement (2020 baseline: 0, 0%) Progress/Status: As of 31 March 2026, cumulatively 117 letters of intent (IBPs) have been signed between 46 PACs (40%) out of 115 target PACs and 83 PAEs.
Cumulatively, ACSEP has achieved 66 PACs over target of 46 PACs signing contract arrangements before the project completion date. As of March 2026, 66 PACs had signed a total of 133 contracts were signed, comprising 59 contract farming agreements and 74 sales agreements including 83 PAEs, Nine companies, one collector and 73 primary schools as consumers/processors).
During Q3 and Q4 2025, 40 business plans were completed with PACs and are ready for further implementation. In Q1 2026, an additional 11 ACs have prepared business plans, bringing the cumulative total to 51 business plans prepared by 51 ACs. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 10 PAEs obtained food safety assurance certificates (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: Despite interest in certification, many PAEs face financial constraints, particularly the high cost of factory upgrades (around $20,000), and limited access to long-term financing. In response, the recent ADB review mission recommended a phased approach, starting with basic certifications such as 5S and CODEX. To date, six PAEs have received technical support from DAI and AVCC to improve infrastructure, documentation, internal controls, and standard operating procedures, preparing them to pursue GHP/HACCP certification. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 30% of cassava PACs adopted disease cleaned materials and at least 30% of mango and cashew PACs adopted improved crop production practices and techniques and at least 30% of poultry farms adopted improved breeds, including at least 30% overall participation of women farmers (2020 baseline: 0%, 0%, 0%) Progress/Status: The Cambodia Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI) plans to provide improved chili and cherry tomato varieties. Seeds are expected to be available for distribution to farmers by 2027. CARDI has identified three vegetable varieties—bitter gourd, melon, and cucumber—for trials to select high-performing varieties and quality seed, based on recommendations from the ADB Review Mission in November 2025.
Nine off-season mango demonstrations and 28 cashew demonstrations focusing on best cultivation practices were initiated, including five training sessions and the provision of agricultural inputs. In Quarter1 ,2026 37 Cassava demonstrations selected and. Demonstrations will continue over two seasons.
The General Department of Animal Health and Production (GDAHP) has selected five cross-breeders to support ACSEP beneficiaries across Kampong Thom, Siem Reap, Oddar Meanchey, Tboung Khmum, and Battambang, with one additional breeder planned for Banteay Meanchey in Q1 2026. Contracts for chicken shed construction have been completed, and agreements between cross-breeders and chick raisers were finalized in Q4 2025. Operational rollout is underway in four provinces, with 235 chickens placed per site, and full provision of feed, vaccines, and equipment—including incubators, electronic scales, egg calipers, labels, and solar systems. GDAHP also delivered training on Good Animal Husbandry and processing practices to 88 participants (37 women). Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: At least 350 farmers (PAC members), of which at least 60% are women, obtained CamGAP certificates (2020 baseline: 0) Progress/Status: A total of 300 farmers (PAC members) has applied for CamGAP certification. Of these, the Plant Protection, Sanitary and Phyto-Sanitary Department (PPSPD) screened, inspected, and audited 150 farmers from 30 PACs across the six former target provinces. These 150 farmers were certified and receive their CamGAP certificates in first quarter 2026. The remaining 150 farmers will be certified in 2027, along with at least 50 new farmers from the new target provinces in 2027. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:

Output: Agricultural value chain linkage and safety strengthened Indicator: Integrated ICT data platform with geo-tagged farm level information built (baseline in 2020: None) Progress/Status: The MAFF Digitalization Strategic Plan, approved on 26 July 2024, requires revision of previously prepared ICT packages, with an updated procurement plan to be submitted to ADB by end-Q1 2026 and an ICT consultant being recruited to support this process with AIDOC. Procurement of end-user computers is progressing following ADB's no-objection (12 December 2025) to the bid evaluation. In parallel, the PMU is assisting AIDOC in recruiting an IT consultant for a 24-month assignment to support the data center and develop a unified MAFF platform; ADB issued no-objection on 16 October 2025 to proceed with advertisement, with contract award expected in Q2 2026 after re-announcement of the ICT consultant position. Data Source: Quarterly project progress reports Actual value:
Value addition of five competitive agricultural value chains in the project areas increased

Products of at least 40 vegetable and/or poultry PACs sold their products at modern retail markets Progress/Status: 164 PACs have been selected as direct beneficiaries, with many involved in vegetable and poultry production.
Training on CamGAP and food safety standards has been provided to farmers and agro-enterprises, which is a prerequisite for accessing modern retail markets. Linking small producers to modern retail outlets is also a considerable leap. It is suggested, even at this stage, that the potential to achieve outcomes will need careful monitoring.
Some PAEs in the target provinces are selling their vegetables and/or chickens to modern retail markets (no quantitative data yet) Data Source: d. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:

Volume of cassava starch production increased to at least 150,000 tons per annum Achievement: 8000 Progress/Status: CARDI has initiated multi-site experiments in five provinces to identify mosaic virus-resistant cassava varieties, and has produced 10,000 disease-free stems via tissue culture so far. Due to limited production capacity, commercial sources will be needed to meet the demand for demonstration farms, which require over 500,000 stems. Based on deep assessment conducted by DAI from March to July 2025, one PAE namely Seung Kimheng Cassava Starch Enterprise is processing cassava starch 50 to 60 tons daily. Data Source: c. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs

Volume of processed cashew increased to at least 15,000 tons per annum Achievement: 2529 Progress/Status: This target is likely to be met.
Foundational activities are underway, including the establishment of inclusive business partnerships (IBPs) and contract farming arrangements between PACs and cashew processing companies.
Demonstration farms for cashew cultivation has commenced since Q3 2025.
Based on deep assessment conducted by DAI from March to July 2025, 2,529 tons of cashew nut has been processed by the 14 selected PAEs in 2025. Data Source: a. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs

Volume of processed mango increased to at least 20,000 tons per annum Progress/Status: Demonstration farms for mango cultivation have started since Q3 2025.
Mango prices have fallen, markets have been lost due to international competition and new markets are not available. Cambodian SPS facilities are not at international standard. Data Source: b. Quarterly project progress reports with inputs from PAEs Actual value:
